name: http-on-http-delivers-the-inbound-body
note: eio_on_http is the only optional callback carrying an inbound payload, so it is the only place ABI §6.1's host-allocates/guest-frees convention is exercised outside process_signals and configure. The scripted id (7) is the async req_id pattern: nothing ties http_request's answer to the later response but the scenario itself, the same as gpio_watch's id in 14_gpio_echo. The body the scenario hands eio_on_http is a real ABI §7.6 {headers, body} map, and the block emits back the exact bytes it was given -- a host that delivered an empty or truncated payload would emit a different, and visibly wrong, batch. eio_stop's balance check is what proves the guest actually freed it: eio_free is an export no engine surfaces to its embedder (§13.1), so the fixture counts its own allocs and frees and refuses to stop unbalanced.
